record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Non-product measures still tractable by QSO theory
record.original_question: In the graph-based construction of QSOs, a product measure over the maximal connected components of the graph yields a non-Volterra QSO reducible to separate Volterra QSOs. Find a probability measure mu on the configuration space that is not such a product measure, but whose corresponding non-Volterra QSO can still be investigated within an established theory of quadratic stochastic operators.

evidence.quote: Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 18. Find a measure µ different from (19) such that the non-Volterra QSO corresponding to µ can be investigated in the framework of a well known theory of QSOs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G=(V,L)$ be a (possibly infinite) graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $L$, and consider a finite "spin" set $\Phi$. The configuration space is $\Omega=\Phi^{V}$, equipped with its product $\sigma$-algebra. For each probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ one can define a quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V_\mu$ on the simplex of probability measures on $\Phi$ associated with the graph $G$ as follows: given two independent configurations sampled from a product distribution determined by a state $x$ on $\Phi$, one applies a local "crossover" rule along the edges of $G$ governed by $\mu$, and $V_\mu(x)$ is the law of the resulting single-site marginal. A QSO is called Volterra if its quadratic coefficients $p_{ij,k}$ satisfy $p_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$, and non-Volterra otherwise.

Reference (product) measure. Suppose the graph $G$ decomposes into maximal connected components $G_1,\dots,G_q$, and let
$$\mu_{\mathrm{prod}}=\bigotimes_{s=1}^{q}\mu_s,$$
where each $\mu_s$ is a probability measure on $\Phi^{V(G_s)}$. It is known that the non-Volterra QSO $V_{\mu_{\mathrm{prod}}}$ generated by such a product measure is reducible to $q$ separate Volterra QSOs, one for each component, and hence its dynamics can be analyzed by the existing theory of Volterra QSOs.

Problem. Exhibit a probability measure $\mu$ on the configuration space $\Omega=\Phi^{V}$ that is not of the product form $\mu_{\mathrm{prod}}$ described above, yet such that the corresponding non-Volterra QSO $V_\mu$ can still be analyzed within an established framework of quadratic stochastic operators (e.g. reduction to Volterra, permuted Volterra, $\ell$-Volterra, or other previously studied classes of QSOs). Describe such a $\mu$ explicitly and indicate the framework in which the associated non-Volterra QSO $V_\mu$ is tractable.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals several related developments in QSO theory (permuted Volterra QSOs, superpositions of Volterra and permuted Volterra operators, parametric families of non-Volterra QSOs, and quadratic non-stochastic operators with "splitted chaos"), but no source was found that directly resolves the specific question of identifying non-product measures $\mu$ on the configuration space whose induced non-Volterra QSO falls within an established QSO framework. The status is therefore inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamical systems generated by superpositions of extremal Volterra and non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators on the two-dimensional simplex are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Related classes of non-Volterra QSOs have been studied via superpositions with Volterra operators, suggesting partial progress on adjacent constructions but not on the specific measure-theoretic problem.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic operators corresponding to permutations
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic stochastic operators corresponding to permutations are introduced and analyzed.
status_evidence.claim: Permuted Volterra QSOs form an established framework into which some non-Volterra QSOs may potentially be embedded.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic non-stochastic operators: examples of splitted chaos
status_evidence.snippet: Examples of non-Volterra-type operators exhibiting splitted chaos behavior are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Other constructions of non-Volterra QSOs exist, but none explicitly correspond to the requested non-product measure.
